text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Parties fighting for the right: Vote-rich Ontario the main battleground as Charest and Manning square-off.
- Tories short on details of cuts: Charest maps a different road to deficit goal.
- Daughter ordered to support parents: Lottery winner loses in court.
- Zaire's parliament votes to oust PM: Government says poll invalid because not enough legislators were present.
- Russia holding on to captured artworks: Part of C$85 billion in war treasure is hidden outside Moscow.
- Abandoned bases ooze pollutants: Radar stations deserted in 1965 still pollute Canada's North.
- Wascana finds white knight: Canadian Oxy's friendly C$1.66-billion takeover bid tops Talisman Energy's hostile one.
- British telecom considers bid for Sprint: Cable & Wireless seeks support from partner in possible C$15 billion offer.
- TSE plans fines for inaccuracies: Committee urges hefty penalties for misleading information.
- Wheat pools drop hostile bid for UGG: Judge rules poison pill can be used.
- C$172-million bid chokes on UGG pill: Manitoba Pool Elevators and Alberta Wheat Pool drop hostile offer after Manitoba judge rules they violated shareholder rights plan.
- White knight CanOxy offers C$2 billion for Wascana.
